page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors clocked at 3.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 48 burstable vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity sits at 192.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5, preserving a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage and operates with a 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile without attached GPU hardware.

Hardware instruction extensions cover advanced cryptographic primitives, vectorization via AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). In synthetic evaluation, the host displays robust single-thread and multi-thread capabilities, registering a PassMark CPU score of 65,038.35 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,732.0. Memory throughput reaches 222.41 GB/sec on large read blocks and 94.88 GB/sec on writes. Furthermore, application-level benchmarks indicate strong results in static web serving at 73.67 GB/sec, Redis SET processing exceeding 64 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations at 24,374.11.

The burstable CPU model offers cost efficiency for workloads that do not saturate all 48 vCPUs continuously, avoiding the expense of dedicated all-core peak compute. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence depends on remote network volumes, alongside a moderate 9 Gbps network interface. Given its wide memory array, fast DDR5 channels, and AMX support, the instance matches well with large application servers, Redis in-memory caches, relational database engines, continuous integration build clusters, and moderate CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 48 burstable vCPUs across 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 192.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory (4.0 GB per core) and a 105 MB L3 cache, supported by AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance provides 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated GPUs or local storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates top-quartile performance in Geekbench multi-core metrics, PassMark database operations, and high-throughput memory transfers up to 222.41 GB/sec. Delivering cost-efficient burst capacity across high vCPU and RAM density, the instance suits enterprise web fleets, large Redis caching tiers, relational database workloads, software compilation, and CPU-driven batch processing.
